```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

[Tessera](https://github.com/ucam-eo/tessera) summarises a year of
Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 observations as an embedding at each 10 m pixel.
geotessera reads those embeddings from Zarr stores into ordinary R objects:
columns added to your points, and `terra` rasters for regions and patches.

This vignette uses the small synthetic store shipped with the package, so it
runs offline. Its values are not real embeddings. Replace
`tessera_example()` with `tessera_store_url()`, or open the default store
with `tessera_open()`, to read the public data.

```{r}
library(geotessera)

gt <- tessera_open(tessera_example())
gt
```

The public stores are opened the same way. Each published dataset is one
inference run, a model version and a variant, and embeddings of different
datasets are unrelated, so use one dataset per analysis:

```{r}
tessera_datasets()[c("version", "variant", "default")]
```

`tessera_open()` with no arguments opens the default v1.1 store. Give
`cache_dir` to keep store metadata and downloaded chunks on disk between
sessions:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gt <- tessera_open(
  tessera_store_url("v1.1"),
  cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("geotessera", "cache")
)
```

## Sampling points

`tessera_sample()` adds one column per band to your points. Points can be
a data frame of WGS84 longitudes and latitudes, or an `sf` or `terra` point
layer in any CRS, which keeps its class.

```{r}
pts <- data.frame(
  site = c("field", "lake", "far away"),
  lon = c(0.0085, 0.0069, 10),
  lat = c(52.0045, 52.0072, 52)
)
tessera_sample(gt, pts, year = 2024)
```

Points without an embedding are `NA`. `tessera_probe()` adds a `status`
column saying why:

```{r}
tessera_probe(gt, pts, year = 2024)[c("site", "status")]
```

For modelling, take the band columns as a matrix:

```{r}
emb <- tessera_sample(gt, pts, year = 2024)
X <- as.matrix(emb[grep("^band_", names(emb))])
dim(X)
```

## Reading a region

`tessera_region()` returns a `SpatRaster` with one layer per band, on the
native UTM grid of the zone holding the centre of the bounds. Bounds are
`c(west, south, east, north)` in degrees, or any `sf` or `terra` object.

```{r, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3}
bbox <- c(0.004, 52.005, 0.013, 52.009)
r <- tessera_region(gt, bbox, year = 2024, bands = 1:3)
r
terra::plotRGB(terra::stretch(r))
```

For regions too large for memory, `tessera_map_region()` applies a
function to row strips of the region:

Bounds given in the zone's CRS are used exactly, so an earlier result
selects the same grid in another year. Prefer this to reprojecting
embeddings, and bring other data to the embeddings' grid instead:

```{r}
r2023 <- tessera_region(gt, r, year = 2023, bands = 1:3)
terra::compareGeom(r, r2023)
```

```{r}
means <- tessera_map_region(gt, bbox, 2024, terra::global, "mean",
                            na.rm = TRUE, strip_rows = 16)
means[[1]][1:3, , drop = FALSE]
```

## Patches across zone boundaries

`tessera_patch()` reads a square of pixels centred on a point, such as an
input tile for a model. The patch lies on the native grid of the point's
UTM zone. Where it crosses into a neighbouring zone, only the pixels beyond
the seam are resampled, by nearest neighbour:

```{r}
p <- tessera_patch(gt, c(0, 52), year = 2024, size_px = 24)
dim(p)
terra::crs(p, describe = TRUE)$code
```

## Exporting GeoTIFFs

`tessera_export_geotiffs()` writes one float32 GeoTIFF per intersecting UTM
zone. Use `dry_run = TRUE` to see the size first:

```{r}
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "tessera")
bbox <- c(-0.0067, 52.0018, 0.0087, 52.0036)
tessera_export_geotiffs(gt, bbox, 2024, out, dry_run = TRUE)
files <- tessera_export_geotiffs(gt, bbox, 2024, out)
basename(files)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(out, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Embedding depths

v2 stores also publish shorter prefixes of each embedding. Choose one with
`depth`:

```{r}
names(gt$depths)
tessera_sample(gt, pts[1, ], 2024, depth = 2)
```
